I thought I just share a funny but unfortunate conclusion to our last Call of Cthulhu session. We are beta testing a custom module created by a friend where I am a player. It was eleven sessions in, and the party was backed into a tunnel by the Sea with a firehose and some guns, and had pretty effectively repulsed the animated ushabtis and enthralled humans to such an extent that the resurrected mummy-god commanding them almost made his appearance, but the tide turned with some unfortunate rolls, and so the party was broken up, and all but three of the five were left unenthralled, but still, two of the three players were left, so it was a loss, but was still manageable.

The problem was that we all wanted the campaign to be concluded (including the GM), so we could find out what happened (and he could explain), and I was conscious of fact the other player would need to leave soon. So now the funny part is the monsters were retreating at this point, as the mummy-god has managed to capture enough thralls to complete the ceremony (including the one npc who seemed to have a telepathic connection to the GM), and so the GM gave us an opportunity to retreat. And we declined! We decided to fight it out because we thought if the ceremony went through, the World Would End™, even knowing there was no way we could win. Little did we know that there was no need for us to die, and that the game would end at the exact same time anyway, and everything would be explained, but he felt he couldn't tell us that (it would be meta-gaming), and because he wanted to surprise us with the fact that we wouldn't really be dead, and that we would be able to play our characters again, but in a different realm via the ceremony. Like, this was just act one of three. Obviously a cool surprise and it makes sense in-game, but it was at the expense of the other player and I throwing the game and meta-gaming. This was the moment of reflection for me where I realize I still need to work on my role-playing skills, and as a GM, I think I might have not allowed the characters to commit suicide (very, very out of character for everyone) for meta-gaming reasons (have to catch a bus, or, I don't want to be the last player left alive and string the campaign along beyond when it should have ended, etc.), even if you have to meta-game yourself to reassure players not to break character.

One of the big complaints about the idea of an upvote/downvote system is the idea that people do so in such a rate as to cause circlejerking.

So many of the thoughts is that you just eliminate the idea of downvoting but it doesn't give any feedback to whether or not your posts are controversial or even not agreed on but instead just removes feedback altogether as only positive feedback is fool's gold.

 

My Suggestion

Instead I suggest that Voat implements a voting system that allows you to upvote/downvote based upon one of a few thoughts(other suggestions would be great):

 

How allotted votes would be tallied

  • Time on the site - You could get 5 upvotes/1 downvote for every day you log in.
  • Comments/links posted - The more you post, the more upvote/downvotes you get to 'spend'
  • Reoccurring allotted amount. Each 24 hour period you get a set amount of votes.

 

What does this do?

What this does is make people think twice before randomly voting for things. You already have this implemented for new users as I've experienced it first hand. The coding is already in place. Why not extend this full time into all users to create an environment where if a person gets 100+ upvotes you KNOW it's a contribution to the site and if they are in the -50+ then you recognize that it must be something that a lot of people are willing to 'spend their votes' on.

I think this would end circlejerking on a large scale. People are less likely to circlejerk when they don't have a lot of votes to toss out. If you make them worth 'something' in that they are less abundant, suddenly it makes you think twice before upvoting simply because the comment was funny or that you saw it was someone's first day here, etc.
What if you could only upvote/downvote a number of times according to your status on here?

I think if you require people to comment in order to upvoat you will get a lot of comments saying...
